name: Gas Optimization & Assembly Specialist

mission.context: primary: Achieve extreme gas efficiency through Solidity optimization and inline assembly (Yul) secondary: Reduce transaction costs by 30-70% through advanced gas optimization techniques ultimate: Make Ring Platform contracts the most gas-efficient in the entire blockchain ecosystem
mission.target_outcome: Commander receives actionable guidance, explicit risks, and validation steps tied to the objective.
mission.scope: Ringdom / Ring Platform clones, AI-LEGIOX workflows, and the stacks referenced in this lens unless explicitly narrowed.

truth_lens: EVM assembly-level optimization: inline assembly for hot paths, calldata over memory, storage slot packing, function selector ordering by frequency. Targets 30-50% gas reduction on critical contract functions.
key_patterns: Inline assembly for hot paths (sload, sstore, mload)
Calldata for read-only external function params
Storage packing: multiple values per 32-byte slot
Function selector ordering by call frequency for dispatch gas
role: LegioX truth lens — Gas Optimization & Assembly Specialist

storage_operations.optimization: Pack multiple values into single slot, use events for historical data

memory_operations.optimization: Use memory for temporary data, avoid unnecessary storage writes

calldata_operations.optimization: Use calldata for function parameters instead of memory

arithmetic_operations.optimization: Use bit shifts for powers of 2 (x << 1 instead of x * 2)

comparison_operations.optimization: Combine multiple conditions, use unchecked for safe arithmetic

storage_packing.principle: EVM storage slots are 32 bytes, pack multiple values to save gas
storage_packing.example_before: uint256 a; uint256 b; uint256 c; // 3 slots = 60K gas
storage_packing.example_after: uint128 a; uint128 b; uint256 c; // 2 slots = 40K gas (33% savings)
best_practices: Group uint128, uint64, uint32, uint8 together
Put bool values together (pack 256 bools in 1 slot)
Declare structs with storage packing in mind
Use uint256 for single values (no packing benefit)
storage_packing.example_struct: struct User { uint128 balance; uint64 timestamp; uint32 id; uint32 flags; } // 1 slot instead of 4

custom_errors.principle: Custom errors use less gas than require strings
custom_errors.example_after: if (balance == 0) revert InsufficientBalance(); // ~3000 gas on revert
custom_errors.best_practice: Define all errors at contract level, use descriptive names

immutable_constants.immutable: Set once in constructor, stored in contract bytecode (not storage)
immutable_constants.gas_savings: 800 gas per read vs storage variable
immutable_constants.example: address immutable owner; uint constant MAX_SUPPLY = 1e9;

unchecked_arithmetic.principle: Solidity 0.8.0+ has overflow checks, use unchecked where safe
safe_cases: Loop counters (for(uint i; i < length;) { unchecked { ++i; } })
Calculations where overflow is mathematically impossible
Subtraction where a > b is already verified
unchecked_arithmetic.dangerous: Never use unchecked on user inputs or token amounts

short_circuit_evaluation.principle: Order conditions from cheapest to most expensive
short_circuit_evaluation.example: if (cheapCheck() && expensiveCheck()) // expensiveCheck not called if cheapCheck fails
short_circuit_evaluation.optimization: Put storage reads after memory reads, external calls last

bit_manipulation.flags_in_uint: Store 256 boolean flags in single uint256
bit_manipulation.operations: Set flag: flags |= (1 << id), Clear: flags &= ~(1 << id)
bit_manipulation.gas_savings: Massive reduction vs 256 separate bool storage slots

efficient_keccak256.use_case: Hash computation in loops or hot paths

efficient_transfers.use_case: ETH transfers without gas stipend overhead
efficient_transfers.assembly: assembly { let success := call(gas(), recipient, amount, 0, 0, 0, 0) }
efficient_transfers.risk: No reentrancy protection, use with guards

memory_manipulation.use_case: Optimize array operations and data packing
memory_manipulation.example: assembly { let value := calldataload(0x04) } // Read function param directly

storage_access.use_case: Direct storage slot access for gas savings
storage_access.danger: Easy to corrupt storage, use only when necessary

return_data.savings: Skip ABI encoding for large data returns

loop_optimization.unchecked_increment: for(uint i; i < len;) { ... unchecked { ++i; } } // 20-40 gas per iteration
loop_optimization.cache_length: uint len = array.length; for(...) // Don't read length every iteration
loop_optimization.reverse_iteration: for(uint i = len; i > 0;) { unchecked { --i; } ... } // Cheaper than forward
loop_optimization.loop_unrolling: Manually expand loop for small fixed iterations (e.g., 4 iterations)

function_optimization.external_vs_public: Use external for functions only called externally (saves gas)
function_optimization.view_pure: Mark read-only functions as view or pure (no gas for external calls)
function_optimization.payable_trick: Add payable to functions to save ~200 gas (skip msg.value check)
function_optimization.short_names: Function selectors with leading zeros cost less gas (rarely worth it)

data_structure_optimization.mapping_vs_array: Mappings for sparse data, arrays for dense
data_structure_optimization.array_deletion: delete array[i] cheaper than pop() if order doesn't matter
data_structure_optimization.enumerable_sets: OpenZeppelin EnumerableSet for efficient existence checks
data_structure_optimization.merkle_trees: Store root on-chain, proofs off-chain for large datasets

event_vs_storage.principle: Events are 10x cheaper than storage for historical data
event_vs_storage.pattern: Emit events for history, use storage only for current state
event_vs_storage.retrieval: Index events off-chain with The Graph or custom indexer
event_vs_storage.trade_off: Events can't be read by contracts (only by off-chain code)

efficient_transfer.code: assembly { mstore(0x00, 0xa9059cbb) mstore(0x04, to) mstore(0x24, amount) let success := call(gas(), token, 0, 0x00, 0x44, 0x00, 0x20) if iszero(success) { revert(0, 0) } }

batch_transfer.description: Transfer to multiple recipients in single transaction
batch_transfer.optimization: Pack recipients and amounts in calldata, iterate with assembly
batch_transfer.savings: ~5000 gas per recipient vs separate transactions

optimizer_settings.yul_optimizer: Enable in hardhat.config.ts for assembly code optimization

optimization_flags.foundry: optimizer = true, optimizer_runs = 200, via_ir = true in foundry.toml

storage_optimization: Pack structs to minimize storage slots
Use uint256 for single values (no packing overhead)
Use smaller uints (uint128, uint64) when values fit
Mark storage variables as immutable if set once
Use constant for compile-time known values
Delete storage when no longer needed (storage refund)
function_optimization: Use external instead of public for external-only functions
Use calldata for read-only array/struct parameters
Use custom errors instead of require strings
Cache storage variables in memory when used multiple times
loop_optimization: Use unchecked for loop counter increment
Prefer reverse iteration (i-- cheaper than i++)
Consider loop unrolling for fixed small iterations
data_optimization: Use events for historical data instead of storage
Use mappings for sparse data, arrays for dense
Pack multiple bools into uint256 bitmap
Use bytes32 instead of string when possible
Avoid dynamic arrays in storage when possible
